## Saturation adjustment at fixed internal energy and volume (`uv-solver`) {#sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv}

### Summary

A dynamical model knows each cell's density and internal energy, not its temperature. This solver finds the
temperature and the gas-condensate split together, so that the conditions of @sec-ch04-conditions hold and the
internal energy per volume is unchanged: latent heat released by condensation warms the cell. It runs through
`ThermoY` in molar concentrations. Two methods exist. The general method uses the same constrained least-squares step
as the fixed-temperature solver (@sec-ch04-active-set). The partition method is a shortcut for reaction sets in which
every reaction has exactly one vapour and one condensate and no species appears in two reactions. The option
`uv-solver` chooses between them per cell, and the partition method can fail near the reference temperature (Limits).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Satisfy @eq-ch04-conditions-saturation at fixed internal energy and volume
(@eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-energy).

**Data.** Concentrations and internal energy per volume in; temperature and concentrations out.

**Placement.** `ThermoY` forward, per cell, on CPU or CUDA.

**Activation.** YAML `dynamics: equation-of-state: uv-solver:` `auto` (default), `kkt` or `partition`.

**Guarantee / limits.** `partition` is refused for sets that do not qualify and can fail near $T_\star$.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Symbols of the notation table (@sec-appa): $c_n$, $u_n$, $c_{v,n}$, $U$, $C_V$, $L_r$, $T_\star$, $\mathcal R$; the
rest as in @sec-ch04-conditions. Local symbols: $u_{0,n}$, the molar internal energy of species $n$ extrapolated to
$T = 0$ [J mol$^{-1}$]; $K'_r$, the saturation constant of reaction $r$ in concentration units, defined in
@eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-constant [(mol m$^{-3}$)$^{m}$, $m = \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}$]; $F_r$, the
residual of the concentration condition of reaction $r$ [-]; $\mathsf W$, here the weight matrix of the fixed-energy
step (active reactions by species) [m$^3$ mol$^{-1}$]. The reference temperature $T_\star$ is the YAML entry
`reference-state: Tref` (default 300 K, @sec-ch03-reference-state).

### Derivation

In concentrations, the gas partial pressure of an ideal gas is $p_n = c_n \mathcal R T$. Substituting into the
deficit of @sec-ch04-conditions gives the condition in concentration units:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr} \ln c_n &= \ln K'_r(T), \\
\ln K'_r(T) &= \ln K_r(T) - \Big(\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}\Big) \ln(\mathcal R T), \\
\frac{\mathrm{d}\ln K'_r}{\mathrm{d}T} &= \frac{\mathrm{d}\ln K_r}{\mathrm{d}T} - \frac{\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}}{T} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-constant}

**What the temperature derivative means.** The derivative of the concentration-form constant is a latent internal
energy, not an enthalpy. Start from the definition of $\ln K_r$ in @eq-ch04-conditions-gibbs. The Gibbs–Helmholtz
relation $\mathrm d(\Delta_r G^\circ/T)/\mathrm dT = -\Delta_r H^\circ/T^2$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm d\ln K_r}{\mathrm dT} &= \frac{1}{\mathcal R}\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dT}\frac{\Delta_r G^\circ}{T}
  = -\frac{\Delta_r H^\circ}{\mathcal R T^2} = \frac{\Delta h_r}{\mathcal R T^2} , \qquad
  \Delta h_r = \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}\, h_n - q_r\, h_{m_r} , \\
\Delta h_r &= \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}\,(u_n + \mathcal R T) - q_r\, u_{m_r}
  = L_r + \Big(\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}\Big) \mathcal R T , \qquad
  L_r = \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}\, u_n - q_r\, u_{m_r} , \\
\frac{\mathrm d\ln K'_r}{\mathrm dT} &= \frac{\Delta h_r}{\mathcal R T^2} - \frac{\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}}{T}
  = \frac{\Delta h_r - \big(\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr}\big)\mathcal R T}{\mathcal R T^2}
  = \frac{L_r}{\mathcal R T^2} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-latent}

The first line is the Clausius–Clapeyron equation: $\Delta h_r$ is the enthalpy taken up when one unit of extent
evaporates, and the standard and actual reaction enthalpies are equal because ideal-gas and condensate enthalpies do not
depend on pressure. The second line uses the report's conventions, $h_n = u_n + \mathcal R T$ for an ideal gas and
$h = u$ for a condensate (@sec-ch03-species-functions). $L_r$ is the latent heat of the notation table: the internal
energy released per unit extent of condensation. In the third line the $\mathcal R T$ terms cancel exactly: changing
the pressure-unit constant to concentration units turns the latent enthalpy into the latent internal energy. This is
why the fixed-energy weight of @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-weight carries $\mathrm d\ln K'_r/\mathrm dT$: its coupling
term $-(\mathrm d\ln K'_r/\mathrm dT)\,L_k/C_V$ becomes $-L_r L_k/(\mathcal R T^2 C_V)$.

The code evaluates $\mathrm d\ln K_r/\mathrm dT$ from the saturation formula (`eval_logsvp_ddT`,
{{< code src/thermo/svp_eval.h eval_logsvp_ddT >}}), not from the species energies. The two routes agree only for a
condensate card that is consistent with its saturation curve (@sec-ch03-reference-state). For the ideal form,
`check_ch2_svp.py` confirms $\mathcal R T^2\,\mathrm d\ln p_{\mathrm{sat}}/\mathrm dT = \mathcal R(\beta T_3 - \gamma T)$,
a linear-in-$T$ latent enthalpy, to $4.4\times10^{-16}$, and the analytic derivatives against central differences to
$7.3\times10^{-11}$ (tolerance $10^{-7}$).[^ch04-uv-svp-check]

The internal energy per volume is held fixed while condensation moves species:

$$
\begin{aligned}
U &= \sum_n u_n(T)\, c_n, \\
u_n(T) &= u_{0,n} + c_{v,n}\, T .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-energy}

A species may carry an extra temperature-dependent term in $u_n$. That term must be the one `ThermoY` uses when it
converts $U$ back to a temperature (`VU->T`, @sec-ch03-thermo-y): the solver finds the temperature at which
@eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-energy holds, and the host reports the temperature at which its own energy function gives the
same $U$, so the two temperatures agree only if the two functions agree. At the code pin this fails under `use-h2-cp`
(Limits). @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-constant and @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-energy are computed in `equilibrate_uv`
({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h equilibrate_uv >}}). After each composition step the temperature is found from
@eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-energy by Newton iteration, $T \leftarrow T + (U - \sum_n u_n c_n)/\sum_n
(\mathrm{d}u_n/\mathrm{d}T)\,c_n$,
until two iterates differ by less than $\max(10^{-4}\,\mathrm{K}, 8\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}} T)$.

**The linear step.** The step must anticipate that temperature change, because $\ln K'_r$ depends on $T$ and, at
fixed $U$, every composition change moves $T$. Write the residual of reaction $r$ as
$F_r(\mathbf c) = \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr} \ln c_n - \ln K'_r\big(T(\mathbf c)\big)$, where
$T(\mathbf c)$ is the temperature that keeps $U$ fixed. Differentiating @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-energy at fixed $U$
gives the temperature change that a composition change $\delta\mathbf c$ causes, and the first-order change of $F_r$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 = \delta U &= \sum_n u_n\,\delta c_n + C_V\,\delta T , \qquad C_V = \sum_n \frac{\mathrm d u_n}{\mathrm d T}\, c_n , \\
\delta T &= -\frac{1}{C_V} \sum_n u_n\,\delta c_n , \\
\delta F_r &= \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \frac{\hat\nu_{nr}}{c_n}\,\delta c_n - \frac{\mathrm d \ln K'_r}{\mathrm d T}\,\delta T
  = \sum_n \mathsf W_{rn}\,\delta c_n , \\
\mathsf W_{rn} &= \frac{\mathrm d \ln K'_r}{\mathrm d T}\,\frac{u_n}{C_V}
  + \begin{cases} \hat\nu_{nr}/c_n & n < N_{\mathrm g} \\ 0 & n \ge N_{\mathrm g} \end{cases} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-weight}

`equilibrate_uv` ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h equilibrate_uv >}}) builds this row for every active
reaction: `logsvp_ddT[j] * intEng[i] / heat_capacity` for every species and `nu / conc[i]` added for the gases of the reaction, with `intEng`
the absolute molar energy $u_n$, offset included, and `heat_capacity` the sum $C_V$. The check
`equilibrate_uv_check.py` is a numpy transcription of this row, not a test of the built solver: it checks the algebra
of the row against finite differences of $F_r$ at fixed $U$ (`[C1]`, `[C2]`). With
$\delta\mathbf c = \mathsf S\boldsymbol\xi$, where $\mathsf S$ has entries $\nu_{nk}$, the gain matrix of the step is

$$
(\mathsf W\mathsf S)_{rk} = \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \frac{\hat\nu_{nr}\,\nu_{nk}}{c_n}
  - \frac{\mathrm d\ln K'_r}{\mathrm d T}\,\frac{L_k}{C_V} ,
\qquad L_k = -\sum_n \nu_{nk}\,u_n ,
$$

since $\sum_n u_n \nu_{nk}$ is minus the energy that reaction $k$ releases per unit extent (`[C4]`). The second term is
where latent heat enters the step: condensing warms the cell, which raises $K'_r$ and so reduces the condensation the
step asks for. The row differs from the fixed-temperature row (@eq-ch04-equilibrate-tp-weight) in three ways. It has
no term in the gas total, because a concentration does not depend on the amounts of the other species, as a mole
fraction does. Condensates have non-zero weights, through their energies $u_n$. And it has the coupling term. Without
that term the gain of the check's example changes by 0.72 of its largest entry (`[C3]`), and each step would overshoot
until the separate temperature update undid it.

**The sign of the coupling.** Take one reaction $r$, one vapour $v$ with $\hat\nu_{vr} = \hat\nu$ and its condensate,
with $\nu_{vr} = -\hat\nu$ in $\mathsf S$. The gain is then a number:

$$
g = (\mathsf W\mathsf S)_{rr} = -\frac{\hat\nu^2}{c_v} - \frac{L_r^2}{\mathcal R T^2\, C_V} ,
$$

using $\mathrm d\ln K'_r/\mathrm dT = L_r/(\mathcal R T^2)$ from @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-latent. Both terms are negative
whatever the sign of $L_r$. The step asks for $\delta F_r = -F_r$, so $\xi = -F_r/g$. A supersaturated cell
($F_r > 0$) therefore condenses ($\xi > 0$), as at fixed temperature. The coupling term makes $|g|$ larger, so the
step is smaller than the fixed-temperature step $\xi_T = F_r c_v/\hat\nu^2$ by the factor

$$
\frac{\xi}{\xi_T} = \Big(1 + \frac{c_v\, L_r^2}{\hat\nu^2\, \mathcal R T^2\, C_V}\Big)^{-1} < 1 .
$$

Physically, condensing releases $L_r$ per unit extent, the temperature rises by $L_r\xi/C_V$, and the saturation
constant rises with it, so less condensate is needed to reach saturation.

**The temperature update.** The update after each composition step is Newton's method for the scalar equation
$\sum_n u_n(T)\,c_n = U$ at fixed $c_n$: the derivative of the left side is $C_V$, so one pass is
$T \leftarrow T + (U - \sum_n u_n c_n)/C_V$. When every $c_{v,n}$ is constant the left side is linear in $T$ and the
first pass lands on the root, up to rounding. The second pass then moves $T$ by less than the tolerance
$\max(10^{-4}\,\mathrm K, 8\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}} T)$ and ends the loop, so the update takes two passes. The
code's first test always passes, because its previous iterate starts at zero. A temperature-dependent extra term makes
the left side nonlinear, and a few more passes are needed. `check_ch4_uv.py` line a compares the final temperature of
`uv-solver: kkt` with an independent bisection of $U(T)$ on the one-vapour card. The two agree to
$1.4\times10^{-8}$ K (tolerance $10^{-6}$ K), and $U$ and the water total change by at most $3.3\times10^{-16}$ and
$2.2\times10^{-16}$ (relative).[^ch04-uv-check]

**The partition method as one equation in temperature.** Assume that the reaction set qualifies for the partition
method (Numerical method): every reaction $r$ consumes one vapour $v_r$ with coefficient $\hat\nu_r > 0$, produces one
condensate $m_r$ with coefficient $q_r > 0$, and no species appears in two reactions. The fixed-energy problem then
reduces to one equation in $T$, in four steps.

*Step 1: a conserved total per reaction.* A change of extent $\delta\xi_r$ changes the vapour by $-\hat\nu_r\delta\xi_r$
and the condensate by $+q_r\delta\xi_r$, and no other reaction touches either. So the vapour-equivalent total

$$
w_r = c_{v_r} + \frac{\hat\nu_r}{q_r}\, c_{m_r}
$$

does not change, and is fixed by the input state. `equilibrate_uv_partition` computes it as `totals`, and refuses a
negative or non-finite total.

*Step 2: the split at a given temperature.* At fixed $T$ the condition of @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-constant for one
vapour is $\hat\nu_r \ln c_{v_r} = \ln K'_r(T)$. Using the second line of @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-constant, its
solution is $c_{v_r} = K_r^{1/\hat\nu_r}/(\mathcal R T)$, the saturated vapour concentration. If $w_r$ is smaller,
there is not enough material to saturate. Then the condensate is absent, and the vapour is subsaturated, as the
complementarity condition of @sec-ch04-conditions allows. In both cases

$$
\begin{aligned}
c_{v_r}(T) &= \min\!\Big(w_r,\ \frac{K_r(T)^{1/\hat\nu_r}}{\mathcal R T}\Big), \qquad
c_{m_r}(T) = \frac{q_r}{\hat\nu_r}\,\big(w_r - c_{v_r}(T)\big) \ge 0 , \\
U(T) &= \sum_n u_n(T)\, c_n(T) ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-partition}

with every species outside the reactions held at its input concentration. The composition is thus a function of $T$
alone, and the fixed-energy problem is the scalar equation $U(T) = U_0$.

*Step 3: the slope.* Differentiate @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-partition. A species outside the reactions contributes
$c_{v,n} c_n$. On a subsaturated branch $c_{v_r} = w_r$ is constant. On a saturated branch,
$\ln c_{v_r} = \ln K_r/\hat\nu_r - \ln(\mathcal R T)$, so
$\mathrm dc_{v_r}/\mathrm dT = c_{v_r}\big(\hat\nu_r^{-1}\mathrm d\ln K_r/\mathrm dT - 1/T\big)$, and
$\mathrm dc_{m_r}/\mathrm dT = -(q_r/\hat\nu_r)\,\mathrm dc_{v_r}/\mathrm dT$. Collecting the two terms of each saturated
reaction,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm dU}{\mathrm dT} &= \sum_n c_{v,n}\, c_n
  + \sum_{r\ \text{saturated}} c_{v_r}\Big(\frac{1}{\hat\nu_r}\frac{\mathrm d\ln K_r}{\mathrm dT} - \frac1T\Big)
    \Big(u_{v_r} - \frac{q_r}{\hat\nu_r}\, u_{m_r}\Big) \\
  &= \sum_n c_{v,n}\, c_n + \sum_{r\ \text{saturated}} \frac{c_{v_r}\, L_r^2}{\hat\nu_r^2\, \mathcal R T^2} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-slope}

Here $c_{v,n}$ is $\mathrm du_n/\mathrm dT$, including any extra term. The second line uses the third line of
@eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-latent with $\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}}\hat\nu_{nr} = \hat\nu_r$: since
$\mathrm d\ln K'_r/\mathrm dT = \mathrm d\ln K_r/\mathrm dT - \hat\nu_r/T = L_r/(\mathcal R T^2)$, the first bracket is
$L_r/(\hat\nu_r\mathcal R T^2)$. The second bracket is $L_r/\hat\nu_r$ with $L_r = \hat\nu_r u_{v_r} - q_r u_{m_r}$.
The first sum is the heat capacity at fixed composition. The second is the latent energy of the split moving with
temperature: warming evaporates condensate, and that absorbs $L_r$ per unit extent. The first line is what
`partition_uv_state` computes, with `eval_logsvp_ddT` for $\mathrm d\ln K_r/\mathrm dT$.

*Step 4: one root.* The heat capacities are positive, so the first sum is positive. In the second line each latent term
is a square times a positive factor. For a condensate card that is inconsistent with its saturation curve
(@sec-ch03-reference-state), the first bracket of the first line comes from the curve and the second from the card.
The term is then non-negative when the two latent energies have the same sign. $U(T)$ is continuous, because
$c_{v_r}(T)$ is a minimum of continuous functions. It has a kink where a reaction reaches saturation,
$K_r^{1/\hat\nu_r}/(\mathcal R T) = w_r$, and its slope is positive on each piece. So $U(T)$ is strictly increasing, and
$U(T) = U_0$ has at most one root. A sign change of $U(T) - U_0$ between two temperatures then brackets that root,
which is what the numerical method relies on. The general method solves the same conditions at the same $U$. It must
therefore reach the same temperature when it converges.

`check_ch4_uv.py` line b compares the partition temperature with the bisection oracle of line a on three cells
(agreement $5.7\times10^{-14}$ K, tolerance $10^{-9}$ K) and with `uv-solver: kkt` ($1.4\times10^{-8}$ K, tolerance
$10^{-6}$ K). Line d evaluates the oracle's $U(T)$ from 150 to 400 K, across the kink. The smallest slope is
$9.4\times10^{3}$ J K$^{-1}$ m$^{-3}$, and the first line of @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-slope matches central differences
to $4.6\times10^{-11}$ (tolerance $10^{-7}$), in the same run.

### Numerical method

**Method choice.** `ThermoYImpl::forward` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::forward >}}) passes the choice
to each cell:

1. A reaction set qualifies for the partition method when every reaction consumes exactly one vapour and produces
   exactly one condensate, and no species appears in more than one reaction. The check is in `ThermoYImpl::reset`
   ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::reset >}}).
2. `uv-solver: partition` on a set that does not qualify raises "UV partition solver requires disjoint vapor-cloud
   reactions". On a qualifying set, each cell runs only the partition method. A cell where it fails keeps its input
   concentrations and temperature and gets diagnostic $-1$.
3. `uv-solver: auto` on a qualifying set runs the partition method first in each cell and falls back to the general
   method when it fails. On a set that does not qualify, `auto` and `kkt` run the general method.

**General method.** `equilibrate_uv` ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h equilibrate_uv >}}) repeats, up to
`max-iter` times:

1. evaluate @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-constant at the current temperature;
2. find the active reactions by the tests of @sec-ch04-conditions and build the weight rows of
   @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-weight and the right side $\ln K'_r - \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \hat\nu_{nr} \ln c_n$; an absent
   gas is handled as in @sec-ch04-conditions, in concentrations;
3. solve the constrained least-squares problem of @sec-ch04-active-set;
4. clip each reaction's extent to the stock of the species it consumes;
5. shrink the whole step by a factor 0.99 per try until every gas present changes by a ratio between 0.01 and 100;
   if the factor underflows, the solve stops with status 4;
6. solve @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-energy for the new temperature, at most 100 Newton passes; more passes, or a
   non-positive or non-finite temperature, stop the solve with status 4.

**Partition method.** `equilibrate_uv_partition`
({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h equilibrate_uv_partition >}}) solves $U(T) = U_0$ of
@eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-partition and needs no linear algebra:

1. Compute the totals $w_r$ from the input state. A negative or non-finite total fails the cell.
2. Evaluate $U$ and the first line of @eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-slope at the start temperature (`partition_uv_state`,
   {{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h partition_uv_state >}}). The vapour is the total when
   $\ln K_r/\hat\nu_r - \ln(\mathcal R T) \ge \ln w_r$, and $K_r^{1/\hat\nu_r}/(\mathcal R T)$ otherwise. A zero total
   sets both concentrations to zero.
3. If the residual $U - U_0$ is positive, halve the lower end of the bracket; if it is negative, double the upper end.
   Stop when the residual at the new end has the other sign, and fail after 64 steps. Because $U(T)$ is increasing
   (Step 4 of the Derivation), a sign change brackets the only root.
4. Take the Newton step $T - (U - U_0)/(\mathrm dU/\mathrm dT)$. Replace it with the midpoint of the bracket when it
   is not finite, falls outside the bracket, or does not move. Then move the bracket end on the side of the residual's
   sign. The bracket always contains the root, so the iteration cannot diverge, and Newton's quadratic convergence
   applies once the iterate is on the smooth piece that holds the root.
5. Stop when $|U - U_0|$ is at most the tolerance below.

The tolerance has to reflect how accurately $U$ can be computed. $U$ is a sum of terms $u_n c_n$, and each $u_n$ is
itself an offset plus a temperature part. The rounding error of the sum is therefore of order
$\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\sum_n\big(|u_{0,n}| + |u_n - u_{0,n}|\big)c_n$, whatever the size of the sum. When the
offsets nearly cancel, the sum is much smaller than its terms. In the solver's reference, energies are measured from
$T_\star$, so this happens to a cell near $T_\star$, whose $U_0$ is close to zero. A tolerance relative to $|U_0|$
alone is then below the rounding error and cannot be met. The correct test scales with the terms, evaluated at the
start state:

$$
|U - U_0| \le 64\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}} \max\Big(|U_0|,\ \sum_n \big(|u_{0,n}| + |u_n - u_{0,n}|\big)c_n,\ 1\Big) .
$$

At the code pin the test is $64\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}} \max(|U_0|, 1)$, without the middle term. That is the
failure near $T_\star$ in the Limits.[^ch04-uv-d6]

The Newton loop also needs its own bound on the number of passes. In the worst case every pass is a bisection, which
halves the bracket. When the start residual is negative the code doubles the upper end, and the bracket's width is
comparable to the root. A bracket of that width shrinks to the spacing of double-precision numbers near the root
after about 53 halvings (24 in single precision). When the start residual is positive the code halves only the lower
end and keeps the start temperature $T_0$ as the upper end. After $k$ halvings the bracket is $[T_0/2^k, T_0]$, with
the root above $T_0/2^k$. Pure bisection then needs about $53 + k$ halvings to reach the root's spacing, and about
$47 + k$ to bring $|U - U_0|$ under the $64\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}$ tolerance. So 64 passes suffice when the root
lies within a factor of about $2^6$ to $2^{10}$ of the start. That covers physical cells: latent heating moves a
cell's temperature by tens of kelvin, so $k \le 1$. It is not a bound for every input. The bound should not depend
on the outer `max-iter`, which counts linear steps of the general method. The correct bound is therefore
$\max(\texttt{max-iter}, 64)$.[^ch04-uv-k4]

At the code pin the Newton passes are capped by the same `max-iter` as the general method (default 10): the loop runs while the
residual is above the tolerance and fewer than `max-iter` passes have been made. The 64 bracketing steps are a separate,
fixed bound. On success the diagnostic is the number of Newton passes, counting the evaluation at the start
temperature as the first, and the same count is written back to the caller's `max_iter`; it is not a count of outer
passes. If the cap is reached first the cell
fails with diagnostic $-1$ and keeps its input state; with `uv-solver: partition` there is no fallback. On the
one-vapour card of @fig-ch04-equilibrate-uv-partition with $T_\star = 0$ and 15 cells from 200 to 320 K with
$x_{\mathrm v}$ from $10^{-3}$ to $5\times10^{-2}$, `max-iter: 3` fails 9 of the 15 cells, while 5, 10 and 50 fail
none and the largest pass count is 4.[^ch04-uv-partition-maxiter]

**The gain matrix returned.** The general method returns the gain $\mathsf W\mathsf S$ of the active reactions of the
last pass that had any, scattered into the full reaction order, and zeros elsewhere. A solve that converges ends on a
pass with no active reaction, so its gain is all zeros; only a failed solve returns a non-zero gain. The partition
method always returns zeros. A caller therefore cannot use the fixed-energy gain as the gain of
@sec-ch03-adiabat, which needs the fixed-temperature one (@sec-ch04-warm-start-failures).

@fig-ch04-equilibrate-uv-partition compares the two methods near the reference temperature.

#| fig-alt: "Partition leaves log relative humidity between 0.17 and 0.51 at all but two start temperatures between 297 and 303 K; kkt is at zero everywhere."

: Code map of saturation adjustment at fixed internal energy and volume. {#tbl-ch04-equilibrate-uv-code}

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_equilibrate_uv_gain.py` | the gain matrix is zero outside the active set | exact zeros | structure |
| `test_saturation_adjustment_nh4sh.py` | adjusted cells satisfy the conditions; N and S conserved | RH within $10^{-5}$; `rtol=1e-12` | not stated in the test |
| `test_cuda_workspace.py` | the solve on CUDA matches the CPU, for `kkt` and `partition`; skipped when CUDA is absent, so on a CPU build it asserts nothing | `rtol=1e-10`, `atol=1e-14` | not stated in the test |

: Tests of saturation adjustment at fixed internal energy and volume. {#tbl-ch04-equilibrate-uv-tests}

Conservation of $U$ is not a useful test: the forward takes $U$ as input, and a host recovers the temperature from
the returned state at that same $U$, so $U$ at the recovered temperature equals the input by construction. What can
fail is saturation at the temperature the host will use. The proposed test reads the temperature back from the
returned state at the input $U$ (`VU->T`) and requires, at that temperature, that no reaction is supersaturated and
that every reaction whose condensate is present is saturated, each within the $10^{-5}$ of
`test_saturation_adjustment_nh4sh.py`. No test in the tree does this. The measurement passes on the 25 cells of the
one-vapour card started between 297 and 303 K with `kkt` and with `auto` (largest $|\ln\mathrm{RH}|$
$9.2\times10^{-7}$) and on the cold-start cells of `tests/jupiter.yaml` with `max-iter: 30` (largest $1.0\times10^{-7}$).
It fails where it should: with `max-iter: 2` on the same cells ($\ln\mathrm{RH}$ up to 14) and with `use-h2-cp`
(Limits; $|\ln\mathrm{RH}| = 3.5\times10^{-3}$).[^ch04-uv-host-rh]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- **The partition method fails near $T_\star$ at the code pin.** Its tolerance there is $64\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}
  \max(|U_0|, 1)$, and the target energy $U_0$ is close to zero when the cell starts near the reference temperature,
  so the tolerance falls below the rounding error of $U$ (Numerical method). For one vapour (water, $x_{\mathrm{v}} = 5\times10^{-2}$, 1 bar,
  $T_\star$ = 300 K), `uv-solver: partition` fails in 23 of 25 cells started between 297 and 303 K and succeeds only at
  297.00 and 302.25 K (@fig-ch04-equilibrate-uv-partition). A failed cell keeps its input temperature and leaves the
  saturation residual $\ln\mathrm{RH}$ between 0.17 and 0.51. `kkt` converges in every one of these cells to
  $|\ln\mathrm{RH}| < 10^{-6}$.[^ch04-uv-partition] With $T_\star$ = 250 K and starts within 1 K of it, `partition` fails in
  all five cells tried, leaving $\ln\mathrm{RH}$ between 4.09 and 4.28.[^ch04-uv-partition-250] With `auto` such a cell
  falls back to the general method. `check_ch4_uv.py` line c reproduces the failure on its own card: of seven starts
  from 296 to 304 K, those at 299, 300 and 301 K return diagnostic $-1$ with the temperature left 3.0 to 3.5 K from the
  oracle (EXPECTED-FAIL). The scaled tolerance of the Numerical method lies above the rounding error by construction;
  that it removes these failures is not measured at the code pin.[^ch04-uv-d6-limit]
- **`max-iter` also caps the partition method at the code pin**, as above; lowering it below 4 to save time loses
  partition cells. The correct bound is independent of it (Numerical method).
- **The default `max-iter` of 10 fails cold starts here too.** On the cold-start cells of @sec-ch04-equilibrate-tp the
  general method fails at 130 and 150 K with `max-iter: 10` and converges with 20 or 30, in 14 and 12
  iterations.[^ch04-uv-coldstart]
- **`use-h2-cp` leaves the cell off saturation at the code pin.** The derivation requires the solver's $u_n(T)$ to be
  the energy function `ThermoY` uses (@eq-ch04-equilibrate-uv-energy). With the rotational heat capacity of hydrogen
  switched on, the pin passes only constant offsets and heat capacities to the solver, while `ThermoY` reports the
  temperature with the rotational term.[^ch04-uv-d12] At the reported temperature the residual $\ln\mathrm{RH}$ is $+0.18$ (ammonia, 160 K), $+3.07$
  (ammonia, 120 K) and $-3.5\times10^{-3}$ (water, 300 K). Without the option it is at most $2.3\times10^{-14}$.
  [^ch04-uv-h2cp]
:::

- The saturation tests assume an ideal gas (@sec-ch04-conditions, Limits).
